analysis.investment_thesis: Entero is a fast-growing pharma distributor riding India's healthcare consolidation wave with 30% revenue CAGR, but it has never generated positive operating cash flow in 5 years — a fatal flaw for a distribution business. At 47.8x P/E with 3.4% operating margins and persistent cash burn, the story doesn't justify the price.
key_strengths: Revenue CAGR of 30.4% (₹1,350 Cr → ₹5,096 Cr) in 5 years shows real scale-up in fragmented Indian pharma distribution
EBITDA inflecting sharply — ₹26 Cr in 2022 to ₹207 Cr in 2025 (42.6% CAGR), and net profit finally turned positive at ₹107 Cr
Low D/E of 0.25 and ₹229 Cr cash post-IPO provide near-term financial cushion
key_risks: Operating cash flow negative in ALL 5 years (0/5 positive; OCF was -₹77 Cr in 2025 despite ₹107 Cr reported net profit) — working capital is a structural trap
Razor-thin margins (3.4% operating, ~2.1% net) leave zero buffer; any pricing pressure or debtor stress could wipe out profitability instantly
Valuation is stretched at P/E 47.8x and EV/EBITDA 29x for a low-margin distributor — ROE of only 5.63% does not justify the multiple
red_flags: OCF negative every single year for 5 consecutive years — a distributor that can't convert revenue into cash is a red flag Lynch would not overlook
Net profit of ₹107 Cr vs. OCF of -₹77 Cr in FY2025 — massive working capital absorption (receivables/inventory) suggests earnings quality is poor
Equity was negative until FY2022; reserves were negative until FY2024 — profitability is brand new and unproven across a cycle
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Entero is trying to become the FedEx of Indian pharma distribution — aggregating thousands of SKUs and delivering to hospitals, retail pharmacies, and clinics across India. The revenue story is genuinely impressive at 30% CAGR, and the operating leverage is finally showing (EBITDA up 6x in 3 years). The forward P/E of 28.72 implies the market expects another ~65% earnings jump, giving a PEG of roughly 0.9-1.0 — borderline acceptable. But the business narrative breaks down badly at the cash flow level. A distribution company's job is to convert thin margins into reliable cash. Entero has failed at this for five straight years, burning cash even in its best revenue year (OCF -₹77 Cr in FY2025 on ₹5,096 Cr revenue).

Peter Lynch's rule: if the earnings are there but the cash isn't, the earnings are suspect. The gap between ₹107 Cr net profit and -₹77 Cr OCF points to receivables expansion eating the business alive — classic working-capital trap in low-margin distribution. At 47.8x P/E and 29x EV/EBITDA with 3.4% operating margins and ROE of just 5.63%, there is no margin of safety. This is a business I'd put on my watch list and revisit only when OCF turns consistently positive for at least 2 years. Until then, the story is incomplete.
